newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen slightly lower in narrow.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen slightly lower in narrow.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open a little softer Tuesday after finishing with modest gains yesterday in a quiet, featureless session.

In over-the-counter business, September Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $30.20-30.30 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Monday's settlement at $30.44, while September California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $22.70-22.90 against yesterday's close at $22.99.
Market sources said the power complex will likely continue its consolidation pattern with little impetus to test any major technical points.
"Looks like more rangebound trading. We're at pretty good support levels here," a New York futures broker said.
Physical power prices in the Southwest were bolstered by reduced hydroelectric supply from the Northwest this week due to maintenance on the Pacific Intertie transmission system.

The 3,800 megawatt (MW) AC segment of the Pacific Intertie was scheduled to be curtailed to 2,950 MW between 0800-1600 PDT through Friday, while the DC line will be limited to 2,360 over the same period.
During early cash activity, firm peak power prices at PV were assessed at $27.75-28.50 and those at COB $18.50-19.50.
A high pressure ridge building in the West was expected to heat the region's temperatures three to seven degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Friday, meteorologists said.

In its latest six- to 10-day forecast, Weather Services Corp said temperatures would average below normal along the coastal region, near normal further inland and above normal in the eastern part of the Southwest.
The 1,221 MW unit 2 at the Palo Verde generating complex in Arizona continued to coast down toward its refueling outage in September.
The unit, in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 80 percent power early Tuesday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
Separately, NYMEX said yesterday it proposed to change the opening times for the electricity futures contracts beginning Wednesday, Sept 3.
The start time will be changed to 0955 EDT/1355 GMT from 1030 EDT/1430 GMT, pending approval by Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
